issue.title: Both test_ace_and_lsp_include_dispatch_* parity nodes fail under the full parallel lane, pass in isolation
issue.description:
FOUND BY the sase-xz.land agent while consuming `just check-full` monitor 4fvbspmpxjw5
(landing gate for epic sase-xz, file-aware pager syntax highlighting). Every lint gate,
SASE validation, committed plans, and the whole `just test-cost` full suite passed; the
only failing step was the last one, `just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake`, which
promoted these two nodes with no entry in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt.

Two nodes, one root cause, one bead: they co-fail in all three promoting records and
never appear apart.

- tests/test_xprompt_directive_completion_parity.py::test_ace_and_lsp_include_dispatch_directive_when_enabled
- tests/test_xprompt_directive_completion_parity.py::test_ace_and_lsp_include_dispatch_machine_rows_when_enabled

NOT caused by epic sase-xz. Neither promoting head is a sase-xz commit (50b1405f4
"feat(dispatch): launch agents on remote machines" x2 and a0fcc5ade "feat(pager): thread
link context through entry points", which belongs to epic sase-xy), and the ACE/LSP
directive-completion parity path has nothing to do with pager syntax highlighting.

`just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake` is the last gate of `just check-full`, so an
undeclared node here blocks every landing agent that reaches it. This bead is filed so
the nodes can carry a baseline entry with a named owner.

Both tests start a real `sase-xprompt-lsp` subprocess through LspSession and assert that
the `%dispatch` directive rows the LSP offers match ACE's own completion rows while the
remote_dispatch flag is enabled. Leading hypothesis, not proven: the installed
`sase_core_rs` extension or the installed `sase-xprompt-lsp` binary is older than the
sase-core checkout and therefore does not know the `%dispatch` vocabulary that landed
with 50b1405f4. Both records at that head co-fail
`tests/test_check_sase_core_rs_bindings_tool.py::test_dev_extension_exposes_every_collected_name`
and `tests/test_xprompt_directive_contract.py::test_runtime_directive_vocabulary_matches_core_contract`,
which is the exact signature of a stale extension; ready bug sase-v6 documents
`rust-lsp-install` copying from the wrong cargo target dir and exiting 0 after the copy
fails. The a0fcc5ade record, however, was a clean tree with no such co-failure, so
staleness alone may not explain every occurrence.

task_type_fields.evidence:
Also covers, with identical evidence:
`tests/test_xprompt_directive_completion_parity.py::test_ace_and_lsp_include_dispatch_machine_rows_when_enabled`

Three eligible full-lane records (schema 2, at most 5 failures each) across two unrelated
heads and three distinct change sets, with later full runs passing both nodes:

1. 20260907T065345Z-50b1405f4268-812137-full-run.json (head 50b1405f4 "feat(dispatch):
   launch agents on remote machines", dirty, 2 changed files, 5 failures; co-failures are
   test_dev_extension_exposes_every_collected_name, the [%dispatch:] argument-rows
   parametrization, and test_runtime_directive_vocabulary_matches_core_contract).
2. 20260907T070520Z-50b1405f4268-950690-full-run.json (same head and co-failure set, 5
   failures).
3. 20260907T163239Z-a0fcc5ade160-2351814-full-run.json (head a0fcc5ade, clean tree, 3
   failures; the only co-failure is
   tests/main/test_parser_machine.py::test_machine_help_renders_sorted_subcommands_and_defaults_to_list,
   another dispatch-machine surface).

Fail rate: parallel full lane only. Serial isolated rerun of both nodes on the sase-xz
landing tree passed (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:randomly -q <both node ids>` ->
2 passed; 0.18s and 0.06s call). The same tree's `just test-cost` full-suite lane also
passed both nodes. No serial reproduction of the failure.

Related, not duplicate: sase-vl owns the wait-prose node in this same parity file (a
different assertion with different evidence), sase-v6 owns the rust-lsp-install staleness
bug, and in-progress epic sase-rj owns the ACE/LSP directive-completion contract.

payload.description: sase-vl owns the wait-prose node in the same ACE/LSP parity file; different assertion and evidence, same LspSession subprocess mechanism
sase-v6's rust-lsp-install staleness bug is the leading hypothesis for an LSP that does not know the %dispatch vocabulary
sase-rj owns the ACE/LSP directive-completion contract these parity nodes assert
epic sase-xe landed the %dispatch directive vocabulary (50b1405f4) whose head produced two of the three promoting records
